answer: Give every identity a fresh, unique skill task — say, decoding a cipher whose key is derived from a violet-tagged public seed — and grade the result with a hidden test suite instead of a human jury. A Sybil farmer would have to genuinely solve thousands of distinct problems, so the cost of each fake identity is real expert effort, not a copied relic of one solved answer. The credential expires after one epoch, so old passes cannot be stockpiled; the limit is that task generation must stay unpredictable, or attackers will precompute answers.
